# The repositories whose job is to read bytes they did not write, swept daily
# by .github/workflows/vuln.yml beside vulnscan-tools.txt.
#
# WHY A SECOND LIST AND NOT MORE LINES IN THE FIRST: that one is a policy about
# BLAST RADIUS -- the tools that hold the token, refuse a push, or produce the
# figures other decisions are taken from. This one is a policy about EXPOSURE:
# parsers, decoders, filesystem and image readers, and the network-facing
# servers among them. Two different questions, two lists, and either can be
# dropped from the lane without touching the other.
#
# WHAT CHOOSING THIS POPULATION FOUND, 2026-10-31, the first sweep anyone had
# run over it: 58 scanned, 0 unread, 56 clean, and **2 reaching** GO-2026-6860
# (golang.org/x/net, fixed in v0.62.0) -- go-webengine/browserproxy and
# go-webengine/engine. In browserproxy the call paths were
# engineRender -> Engine.RenderWithLinks -> html.Parse and
# run -> http.Server.Shutdown -> html.ParseFragment: the actual job of the
# program, not an init artefact.
#
# ⛔ AND x/net WAS `// indirect` THERE. An indirect requirement is not a floor
# the module declares for itself, so no dependency manager has a version string
# to compare or rewrite: nothing was watching it, and nothing would have. That
# is the whole reason this list exists rather than a Renovate rule.
#
# ⛔ THE REACHING REPOSITORIES ARE NOT THE ONES WITH THE MOST DEPENDENCIES.
# They are the ones whose job is to read untrusted bytes. 56 of 58 clean means
# this population is in good health; the sweep is insurance, not firefighting.
#
# ⛔ A REPOSITORY ADDED HERE MUST BE GREEN FIRST. A lane that is red on its
# first night is not an alarm, it is something people learn to scroll past --
# which is the failure this whole workflow exists to refuse. Run the sweep by
# hand over the new line before committing it.
#
# ⛔⛔ DO NOT ENABLE THIS LANE YET -- 58 UNAUTHENTICATED CLONES TRIP GITHUB'S
# RATE LIMIT. Measured here at 22:31 on 2026-10-31, the same list, the same
# binary, half an hour after a run that read all 58:
#
#   58 listed, 58 scanned: CALLED 0, CLEAN 44, NO-GO 0, UNREAD 14
#   [50/58] UNREAD go-images/gif  could not scan: git clone: exit status 128:
#           fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/go-images/gif.git/':
#           The requested URL returned error: 403
#
# Fourteen failures, every one a clone and not a finding. vulnscan makes no REST
# call per repository -- that claim stands, and it is why this cannot starve the
# budget the Renovate runners spend from -- but the GIT TRANSPORT is rate
# limited too, and an unauthenticated sweep of 58 repositories reaches it. The
# 13-repository tools list does not: it read clean twice tonight.
#
# ⛔ And UNREAD IS NOT CLEAN. vulnscan exits 2, so the lane would be RED for a
# reason that is the SWEEP's and not any repository's -- the precise shape of
# alarm this workflow was written to refuse.
#
# Two ways out, and the choice is a real one rather than an oversight:
#   - SLICE the list across the week, so each night clones a dozen -- under the
#     line, and every repository still seen weekly;
#   - AUTHENTICATE the clones, which raises the limit and gives up the
#     no-credential property this job was built on.
#
# ⛔ AND NOT `-state`, WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO A DIFFERENT QUESTION. It makes a
# sweep RESUMABLE: it records each repository's verdict and skips what it
# already holds, so `-retry-unread` reclones only the ones that failed. That is
# exactly right WITHIN one run -- the 14 clone refusals tonight would have cost
# 14 retries instead of 58 -- and exactly wrong ACROSS nights: a repository that
# was CLEAN yesterday is not clean today if an advisory was published since.
# The code did not change; the DATABASE did, which is the whole reason this runs
# on a clock. Carrying state between nights would turn the lane into a cache of
# yesterday's answers.
#
# So: slice or authenticate for the volume, and `-state` with `-retry-unread`
# inside whichever is chosen, so one refused clone does not cost a whole pass.
# (Verified from tonight's artefacts: the state file holds one verdict per
# repository with its own `scanned_at`. The run that hit the limit had `-json`
# but no `-state`, which is why it recloned all 58.)

# the browser: network in, untrusted HTML parsed
go-webengine/engine
go-webengine/browserproxy
go-webengine/esbuildsandbox
